parts.solution_md:
*Get rid of fractions (by multiplying both sides by **bvR**)* * *

$\begin{gathered} b v R ( \frac{m}{v} - \frac{t}{b} ) & = b v R \times \frac{( m - t )}{R} \\ \\ \frac{b \cancel{v} R m}{ \cancel{v} } - \frac{ \cancel{b} v R t}{ \cancel{b} } & = \frac{b v \cancel{R} ( m - t )}{ \cancel{R} } \\ \\ b R m - v R t & = b v ( m - t ) \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets on the right* * *

$bRm-vRt=bvm-bvt$ * *

*Move all the **m** terms on to one side (for example, by subtracting **bvm** from both sides then adding **vRt** to both sides)* * *

$\begin{array}{rcl} b R m - v R t - b v m & = - b v t \\ b R m - b v m & = v R t - b v t \end{array}$

**[1]**

*Factorise **m** out of the terms on the left* * *

$m ( b R - b v ) = v R t - b v t$

**[1]**

> *Get **m** on its own (by dividing both sides by **bR - bv**)*

$m=\frac{vRt-bvt}{bR-bv}$* ***[1]**

$m=\frac{bvt-vRt}{bv-bR}$* ***is also accepted**

equations.alt: b R m minus v R t equals b v m minus b v t

parts.solution_md:
> *First we want to get rid of the fraction, by multiplying both sides by the denominator*

> *Next, as *$x$* is the subject, we want to get all the *$x$*s to one side of the equation. So add *$x$* to both sides*

**[1]**

> *Now we can factorise out the *$x$

$x(k+1)=2m$

**[1]**

> *Finally we divide both sides by *$(k+1)$* to leave *$x$*on its own*

$x=\frac{2m}{k+1}$** [1]**

parts.solution_md:
*Method 1* 
*Add *$t^{2}$* and subtract *$s$* from both sides of the equation to leave the term in *$t$* on its own.*

$\begin{array}{rcl} s + t^{2} & = k \\ t^{2} & = k - s \end{array}$

**[1]**

> *Square root both sides to get *$t$*. The square root of a number can be positive or negative (because *$( - x ) \times ( - x ) = x^{2}$*) so it is best to write "±" before the square root - but you won't lose marks if you don't do this at IGCSE.*

$\pm\sqrt{k-s}=t$

$t=\pm\sqrt{k-s}\mathrm{or}t=\pm\sqrt{-s+k}$ **[1]**

**At IGCSE, the "±" sign is optional**

*Method 2* 
*Subtract *$k$* from both sides to leave the term in *$t$* on its own.*

$s-k=-t^{2}$

> *Multiply both sides by −1 (reverse the signs of all the terms) to make *$t^{2}$* positive.*

$-s+k=t^{2}$

**[1]**

> *At this stage it's not necessary but it's good practice to write the positive term first.*

$k-s=t^{2}$

> *Finally, square root both sides to get *$t$*. The square root of a number can be positive or negative (because *$( - x ) \times ( - x ) = x^{2}$*) so it is best to write "±" before the square root - but you won't lose marks if you don't do this at IGCSE.*

$\pm\sqrt{k-s}=t$

$t=\pm\sqrt{k-s}\mathrm{or}t=\pm\sqrt{-s+k}$ **[1]**

**At IGCSE, the "±" sign is optional**

parts.solution_md:
*"Make *$P$* the subject" means write it as *$P=...$* (with no *$P$*'s on the right-hand side)* 
*Get rid of the denominator 100 (by multiplying all terms on both sides by 100)* * *

$100A=100P+PRT$

**[1]**

*Get one *$P$* on its own (by factorising out a *$P$* from both terms on the right)* * *

$100 A = P ( 100 + R T )$

**[1]**

*Make *$P$* the subject by dividing both sides by *$( 100 + R T )$

$\frac{100A}{100+RT}=P$

$P=\frac{100A}{100+RT}$** [1]** 
**The following is not accepted as the final answer as there is a fraction in the denominator:** $P=\frac{A}{1+\frac{RT}{100}}$

equations.alt: 100 A equals 100 P plus P R T

parts.problem_md:
Make *y* the subject of the formula

$t=\frac{2-3y}{y+2}$
parts.solution_md:
*Remove the fraction (by multiplying both sides by **y** + 2)* * *

$t ( y + 2 ) = 2 - 3 y$

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets (by multiplying the terms inside by **t**)* * *

$ty+2t=2-3y$ * *

*Collect the **y** terms on one side (for example, by adding 3**y** to both sides then subtracting 2**t **from both sides)* * *

$\begin{gathered} t y + 2 t + 3 y & = 2 \\ t y + 3 y & = 2 - 2 t \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

*Factorise** y** out of the terms on the left* * *

$y ( t + 3 ) = 2 - 2 t$

**[1]**

*Get y on its own (by dividing both sides by **t** + 3)* * *

$y=\frac{2-2t}{t+3}$* ***[1]**

$y=\frac{2t-2}{-t-3}$** is also accepted**

equations.alt: t y plus 2 t equals 2 minus 3 y
